scientific_object: Representation-invariant skill evolution: when semantically equivalent skill identities are also control handles and persistent evidence/lifecycle keys, an exact identity refinement can alter both immediate semantic selection and future skill survival even though capability content and post-selection semantic feedback are unchanged.
one_sentence_insight: In a self-evolving skill library, identity can act twice: once when the system selects what to use, and again when it decides where evidence accumulates; exact semantic splitting therefore creates two orthogonal representation channels—selection duplication and credit fragmentation—that require separate quotient interventions.

why_r2_is_deeper_than_r19.r19: R19 primarily audits static selection/exposure realizability and shows one bounded representation-to-retrieval-to-behavior manifestation.
why_r2_is_deeper_than_r19.r2: R2 identifies a persistent post-selection update mechanism in released Skill-SP: identical semantic feedback is partitioned across per-ID sufficient-statistic containers before a nonlinear lifecycle gate, changing the future active library. The effect remains after selection/retrieval is removed and has an exact multiplicity/evidence phase law.
why_r2_is_deeper_than_r19.not_a_rename: The R2 residual makes an ex-ante prediction R19 does not: under fixed semantic feedback, a k-way exact identity refinement delays full semantic-class retirement from N=M to N=kM, producing a fragmentation window M<=N<kM and lag (k-1)M.

formal_model.semantic_quotient: Let pi map skill identities i to semantic classes c. Exact refinement changes the identity partition while preserving pi-level capability content.
formal_model.selection_channel: Identity probabilities p_t(i) induce semantic selection mass P_t(c)=sum_{i:pi(i)=c} p_t(i). Representation-invariant selection requires P_t(c) to be unchanged by exact refinement. R19 support geometry and R* remain the general package-control audit for this channel.
formal_model.credit_state: Each identity i stores persistent sufficient statistics s_{t,i} in an aggregation space with operator ⊕. The semantic class state is S_{t,c}=⊕_{i:pi(i)=c} s_{t,i}.
formal_model.lifecycle_gate: Let g(s)=1 denote a lifecycle decision such as retirement. Native identity-local evolution retires the semantic class only when every refined identity passes the gate, AND_i g(s_i); semantic quotient-credit applies g after aggregation, g(⊕_i s_i).
formal_model.credit_invariance_criterion: Representation-invariant lifecycle evolution requires g(⊕_i s_i)=AND_i g(s_i) for every exact refinement partition relevant to the semantic class.
formal_model.skillsp_phase_law: For retirement-eligible evidence, additive attempt count, and per-ID threshold M, canonical/quotient retirement occurs at N>=M; a balanced k-way exact refinement fully retires at N>=kM. The fragmentation window is M<=N<kM and retirement lag is (k-1)M.
formal_model.organizing_commutation_rule: At the whole-loop level, semantic projection after update should agree with update after semantic projection. This quotient/commutation statement is used only as an organizing criterion; generic lumpability/homomorphism is not claimed as novelty.

mechanism_decomposition.design: 2x2: selection handling {native, semantic quotient} x credit/lifecycle handling {native per-ID, semantic quotient}.
mechanism_decomposition.canonical_reference: One focal semantic skill plus one background skill: focal semantic selection probability 1/2; eight easy feedback records retire the focal identity.
mechanism_decomposition.native_native: Exact split2 gives focal selection probability 2/3 and partitions eight feedback records 4/4, leaving both focal identities active.
mechanism_decomposition.quotient_selection_native_credit: Selection probability returns to 1/2 but the lifecycle defect remains.
mechanism_decomposition.native_selection_quotient_credit: Lifecycle decision returns to canonical retirement but the 2/3 immediate selection defect remains.
mechanism_decomposition.quotient_both: Both semantic selection and lifecycle endpoints match the canonical representation.
mechanism_decomposition.conclusion: Selection duplication and credit fragmentation are separable causal channels; repairing either alone is insufficient for full representation invariance.

iclr_closed_loop_story: 1. Phenomenon: exact semantic identity refinement changes a released self-evolving controller even though capability content is unchanged; identity is therefore not harmless metadata.
2. Latent mechanism: the identity is used on two control surfaces—selection mass and persistent evidence/lifecycle state. The second surface survives after selection is mechanically removed.
3. Mechanism law: per-ID evidence partition before a nonlinear lifecycle gate creates a closed-form fragmentation window M<=N<kM and multiplicity-dependent retirement lag (k-1)M.
4. Causal decomposition: a 2x2 quotient intervention separates selection duplication from credit fragmentation; fixing one leaves the other, fixing both restores both canonical semantic endpoints.

5. Cross-system structure: SkillsVote independently partitions evolvable feedback by linked skill identity before updater calls; RethinkSkill provides a close feedback-dynamics control that lacks the parallel-identity structure.

6. Boundary and consequence: AutoSkill P19 shows one behavioral manifestation, but the R19 heldout STOP and unreleased Skill-SP evolved state forbid claims of task-general behavior or natural prevalence. The paper closes at a representation-invariant control principle, not utility improvement.
